body: claimed: Codex (m3) · 2026-11-24T07:48Z · branch mkinney:issue/3593-tangency-slice-cost · plan: measure tangency in release; cut the per-slice cost with an exact slice that gives the same region, pinned by an equivalence test

Release measurement on upstream/main 415440375. I added temporary timers and did not change the code. I did not push a branch.

Command: `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --test pocket_pass_start <test> -- --ignored --exact --nocapture`

| Test | Moves | Distinct slices | Tangency time | Test time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge_light` (Waterline) | 9261 | 1709 | 1.75 s | 4.8 s |
| `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` (Waterline + OffsetRings) | 9261 + 10950 | 1709 + 1569 | 1.76 s + 1.67 s | 9.5 s |

Where the time goes (Waterline, release):
- One slice of the 10668-facet model takes about 0.76 ms. All slices take 1.30 s of the 1.75 s.
- `Region::from_slices` (step 4 of `slice_with`) takes 1.00 s of the 1.30 s. The facet scan, the chord weld and the cycle walk take about 0.30 s.
- The `IndexedSlice` build (#3615) takes 0.19 s. The law itself takes about 0.25 s.

What this means for the possible directions:
- An incremental slice (an active facet set between planes) removes only the facet scan. That is about 0.3 s of the 1.75 s, at most about 17 %. The region normalisation stays.
- A reuse of one slice between two facet-vertex levels changes the section that the law judges. The law is under the safety floor, so I did not do it.
- A real speed-up must make `Region::from_slices` cheaper, or must skip it for loops that it does not change. That is geometry work and needs its own design.

The issue says: "Measure the release build first: if it is seconds there, lower the priority." In release the time is 1.7 s for each operation, so I followed that step. I changed the priority from `P3` to `P8`. This is a speed issue, not a wrong result, and the next step is design work. The heavy and light tests run in release only, so the 34.7 s debug time does not occur in a gate. The maintainer decides if the issue stays open at `P8` or closes as "measured and found small". I removed `claimed`.
